title: Candidate Data Exposure
description: Because candidate records may be over-retained and recruiter accounts broadly privileged, a compromised account could expose resumes and identity documents, causing privacy harm, notification costs, and loss of candidate trust.
causes: Broad ATS export permissions and inconsistent access reviews
Sensitive attachments retained beyond business need
consequences: Candidate identity misuse and loss of confidentiality
Privacy notification and regulatory investigation costs
controls: Assumed: ATS role-based permissions and encrypted transport
Assumed: employee security induction and documented privacy policy
residualBasis: Target only: lower exposure depends on validated least privilege, stronger authentication, retention enforcement, and response exercises; impact remains major because sensitive records remain in scope.

actions.action: Enforce phishing-resistant MFA and restrict bulk exports
Approve retention schedule and test deletion of expired attachments
Run candidate-data incident tabletop and sample access review

title: Consultant Access Not Revoked
description: Because assignment end dates and client offboarding responsibilities may be inconsistent, a former consultant could retain client-system access after departure, enabling unauthorized changes or disclosure and damaging client relationships.
causes: Assignment changes not synchronized with identity records
Unclear division of revocation duties with client teams
Unmanaged shared accounts or long-lived credentials
consequences: Contractual penalties and loss of client confidence
Delayed investigation when account ownership is unclear
controls: Assumed: client sponsors approve initial consultant access
residualBasis: Target only: conditional on client-confirmed revocation, time-limited access and sampled evidence. Reduced impact assumes effective client scoping; client-owned controls have not been verified.

actions.action: Establish a client responsibility matrix and revocation SLA
Reconcile active assignments against client access attestations
Test end-date alerts and require revocation evidence

title: Recruiter Impersonation and Payment Fraud
description: Because recruiter identities and payment instructions may be insufficiently authenticated, an impersonator could redirect consultant payments or solicit candidate fees, creating financial loss and reputational harm.
causes: Spoofed email domains and social profiles
Bank-detail changes accepted through email alone
Limited awareness of fee scams among candidates
consequences: Candidate financial harm and reputational damage
controls: Assumed: dual approval for payment runs
Assumed: public notice that candidates are never charged placement fees
residualBasis: Target only: callback verification and payment limits must be tested before relying on reduced likelihood or loss magnitude. Email authentication alone cannot prevent lookalike-domain scams.

actions.action: Require verified callback for bank-detail changes
Deploy and monitor SPF, DKIM and enforced DMARC
Publish verified recruiter contact guidance and scam reporting channel

title: ATS/CRM Service Disruption
description: Because recruiting depends on a hosted ATS/CRM and recovery processes may be untested, a supplier outage or integration failure could interrupt candidate matching and client delivery, resulting in missed placements and revenue loss.
consequences: Lost revenue and client service breaches
Manual-workaround errors and duplicated candidate records
controls: Assumed: supplier status notifications and support agreement
Assumed: restricted access to periodic business-data exports
residualBasis: Target only: assumes restoration and a privacy-preserving manual workflow meet calibrated recovery objectives in an exercise. Supplier availability remains outside direct control.

actions.action: Define recovery time and recovery point objectives with business owners
Exercise export recovery and secure temporary candidate scheduling
Review supplier resilience evidence and escalation contacts

title: Screening Bias and Hiring Compliance
description: Because screening criteria and automated recommendations may lack consistent fairness review, qualified candidates could be excluded unfairly or without required notices, resulting in discrimination complaints, regulatory exposure, and loss of client trust.
causes: Unreviewed vendor screening models and accessibility barriers
Insufficient jurisdiction-specific notice and appeal procedures
consequences: Loss of trust and reduced diversity of candidate pools
controls: Assumed: human review of shortlisted applicants
Assumed: equal-opportunity policy and basic recruiter training
residualBasis: Target only: subject to documented job-related criteria, counsel review, accessible appeals, and legally appropriate outcome testing. Major impact remains plausible; a human reviewer alone does not establish fairness.

actions.action: Approve structured, job-related screening criteria and review exceptions
Review notices, accommodations and appeal process with qualified counsel
Assess vendor evidence and design lawful fairness monitoring
